name: verbatim_string_double
why: the corpus holds no @"..." at all, so VerbatimStringDouble and the doubled-quote unescape are graded by nothing else

name: verbatim_string_single
why: one corpus file has @'...'; the unparser puts the doubled quote back, so it is worth pinning directly

name: verbatim_string_field
why: a verbatim string as a field name is an ObjectFieldStr whose Expr1 is the literal

name: tailstrict
why: one corpus file uses tailstrict; TailStrictFodder is read only when TailStrict is set

name: tailstrict_fodder
why: TailStrictFodder with something in it, which nothing in the corpus reaches
source:
local f(x) = x;
f(1) /* before */ tailstrict

name: importbin
why: one corpus file uses importbin

name: import_all_three
why: Import, ImportStr and ImportBin side by side, each with a LiteralString child

name: visible_field
why: ::: appears in two corpus files; all three Hide values in one object

name: super_sugar_all_hides
why: +: with each visibility, which sets both SuperSugar and Hide

name: slice_colon_only
why: a[:] - every index nil and StepColonFodder empty, so no step colon is written

name: slice_double_colon_no_step
why: a[::] parses to exactly the same AST as a[:]: the lexer makes '::' one operator token, so the parser's '::' branch fills fodders[0] and bumps colonsConsumed by 2, never assigning fodders[1]. So jsonnetfmt rewrites a[::] to a[:]. This snippet pins that collapse

name: slice_every_slot_commented
why: an interstitial in each of LeftBracketFodder, EndColonFodder, StepColonFodder and RightBracketFodder at once

name: index_dot_commented
why: on e.f, LeftBracketFodder is the fodder before the '.' and RightBracketFodder is the fodder before the id - one slot, two jobs

name: index_bracket_commented
why: on e[e], the same two slots mean the fodder before '[' and before ']'

name: super_dot_commented
why: SuperIndex spells the same doubling DotFodder / IDFodder

name: super_bracket_commented
why: super[e], where IDFodder is the fodder before the ']'

name: in_super
why: InSuper, four corpus files

name: in_super_commented
why: InFodder and SuperFodder both filled

name: objcomp_two_fors_two_ifs
why: ForSpec.Outer chaining plus IfSpec attachment, which the unparser walks outermost-first
source:
{
  ['k' + x]: y
  for x in ['a', 'b']
  if x != ''
  for y in [1, 2]
  if y > 0
}

name: arraycomp_two_fors_two_ifs
why: the same chaining in an array comprehension
source:
[
  x + y
  for x in [1]
  if x > 0
  for y in [2]
  if y > 1
]

name: arraycomp_trailing_comma
why: ArrayComp.TrailingComma and TrailingCommaFodder, which only exist on a comprehension

name: objcomp_trailing_comma
why: ObjectComp.TrailingCommaFodder

name: forspec_commented
why: an interstitial in ForFodder, VarFodder, InFodder and IfFodder

name: function_expr_defaults_trailing_comma
why: a Function node with a defaulted parameter and a trailing comma

name: method_sugar
why: a field method: Method carries the parens and parameters, and has no opening fodder of its own

name: local_fun_bind
why: LocalBind.Fun, the same shape as a method and equally fodder-less at the front
source:
local f(x, y=1,) = x + y;
f(1)

name: params_commented
why: NameFodder, EqFodder and CommaFodder on parameters

name: local_multiple_binds
why: several binds, so CloseFodder is the fodder before a ',' for all but the last and before the ';' for it

name: object_field_kinds
why: ObjectFieldID, ObjectFieldStr, ObjectFieldExpr, ObjectLocal and ObjectAssert in one object
source:
{
  local x = 1,
  assert true,
  assert x == 1 : 'msg',
  a: 1,
  'b': 2,
  "c": 3,
  ['d' + 'e']: 4,
}

name: object_local_method
why: a local method inside an object

name: object_assert_no_message
why: ObjectAssert with Expr3 nil, so OpFodder is never read

name: object_every_slot_commented
why: Fodder1, Fodder2, OpFodder and CommaFodder on one computed field, plus CloseFodder

name: object_empty_commented
why: CloseFodder on an object with no fields, where the unparser passes crowded=false

name: array_empty_commented
why: the same for an array

name: array_every_slot_commented
why: CommaFodder on each element and CloseFodder after a trailing comma

name: apply_named_and_positional
why: positional then named arguments, a trailing comma, and FodderLeft / FodderRight
source:
local f(a, b) = a + b;
f(1, b=2,)

name: apply_every_slot_commented
why: FodderLeft, each CommaFodder, NameFodder, EqFodder and FodderRight

name: apply_brace
why: ApplyBrace, e { }, which the formatter may rewrite to e + { } under AddPlusObject

name: assert_expr_with_message
why: a standalone Assert with ColonFodder and SemicolonFodder

name: assert_expr_no_message
why: Assert with Message nil

name: conditional_commented
why: ThenFodder and ElseFodder

name: conditional_no_else
why: Conditional with BranchFalse nil, so ElseFodder is never read

name: error_expr
why: Error

name: parens_commented
why: Parens.CloseFodder, and the inner expression unparsed with crowded=false

name: unary_ops
why: all four unary operators

name: dollar
why: Dollar

name: self
why: Self

name: binary_left_recursion
why: a left-recursive chain: the leading fodder must be stored on the leftmost leaf, not on the outermost Binary

name: binary_op_fodder
why: OpFodder on each operator of a chain

name: all_binary_ops
why: every binary operator, so BopMap is graded rather than assumed

name: number_original_string
why: LiteralNumber keeps OriginalString, so these are four different programs to the formatter

name: block_string
why: a block string, with BlockIndent and BlockTermIndent

name: block_string_chomped
why: a block string whose value does not end in a newline, which the unparser writes as |||-

name: paragraph_and_interstitial_at_top
why: a multi-line C comment at the start of a file, which FodderAppend precedes with a synthetic LineEnd - the exact shape two hand-written lexer expectations got wrong

name: line_end_comment_slots
why: line-end comments in fodder slots, which the unparser always precedes with exactly two spaces

name: literals
why: LiteralNull, LiteralBoolean and both fully escaped string kinds in one place, so no node kind depends on the corpus happening to contain one

name: named_arg_eq_fodder_is_dropped
why: NamedArgument.EqFodder is filled by the parser and never read by the unparser, so this comment is dropped from the output - the port must store it anyway or the AST will not match
source:
local f(a, b) = a + b;
f(1, b /* dropped */ = 2)

name: slice_step_colon_fodder_without_step
why: the only shape where the unparser's `Step != nil || len(StepColonFodder) > 0` can take its second branch: a comment before a step colon that has no step after it. With no passes it round-trips as written; under DefaultOptions NoRedundantSliceColon moves the fodder to the front of RightBracketFodder and drops the colon

name: slice_step_colon_no_fodder_no_step
why: a step colon consumed with no fodder before it, which leaves StepColonFodder empty - so the unparser cannot tell a[1:2:] from a[1:2] and writes the latter. The pair with the snippet above is what makes the emptiness of that slot meaningful rather than incidental
